what_its_for: Plerixafor is used to help move stem cells from your bone marrow into your bloodstream so they can be collected and stored. These stem cells are then used in a stem cell transplant to treat certain blood cancers, such as multiple myeloma or non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. It is always used together with another medicine called G-CSF (filgrastim).
how_to_take: Plerixafor is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your belly area, upper arm, or thigh. A nurse or doctor will give you this injection in a clinic or hospital setting. You will not inject this medicine yourself at home. The injection is given about 11 hours before your stem cell collection procedure (called apheresis) is scheduled to begin.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your actual body weight. The usual dose is 0.24 mg per kilogram of body weight, given once a day for up to 4 days in a row. Your dose may be lower if you have kidney problems. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing instructions.
missed_dose: Because plerixafor is given by a healthcare provider in a clinic, a missed dose is unlikely. However, if your appointment is missed or rescheduled, contact your transplant team right away. Your stem cell collection schedule may need to be adjusted, so do not skip or delay any appointments without talking to your doctor first.
storage: Plerixafor is stored and handled by your healthcare team. If you are given any information about storage, keep it at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from light, heat, and out of reach of children. Do not freeze the medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or lightheaded after receiving your injection, as plerixafor can sometimes cause dizziness. Avoid getting up too quickly from a lying or sitting position, as this medicine can cause a drop in blood pressure. Let your care team know before taking any new prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, or herbal supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: severe stomach pain or bloating (this could be a sign of an enlarged spleen), sudden pain in the left shoulder or upper left belly area, a skin rash, hives, or signs of an allergic reaction (swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, rapid heartbeat), fainting or severe dizziness, or numbness or tingling around the mouth. Also tell your doctor if you have unusual bruising, bleeding, or any signs of infection such as fever or chills.
when_it_works: Plerixafor begins working quickly. It starts releasing stem cells into your bloodstream within a few hours after the injection, which is why it is timed carefully before your stem cell collection procedure. Your medical team will check your blood to make sure enough stem cells have been released before collection begins.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your dose will be reduced if your kidneys are not working well. Make sure your doctor knows about any kidney disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Plerixafor may harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. Use effective birth control during treatment. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, so extra caution is advised when standing up. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
